title: A bill to amend section 1214 of title 5, United States Code, to provide for stays during a period that the Merit Systems Protection Board lacks a quorum.
official_summary:
This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on May 25, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

This bill provides that if the Merit Systems Protection Board lacks the number of members required to constitute a quorum, any remaining member of the board may, upon request by the Special Counsel, extend the period of any stay of any personnel action granted.

summary.headline: This law lets a remaining member of the Merit Systems Protection Board extend certain personnel-action stays when the board lacks a quorum.
summary.what_it_does: The Merit Systems Protection Board hears appeals from federal employees about personnel actions such as firings or demotions. A stay pauses such an action while the case is reviewed. This law says that if the board does not have enough members to make a quorum, any remaining member may extend the length of a stay when the Special Counsel asks. The change applies only during the time the board lacks a quorum.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees facing personnel actions such as removal or demotion
who_it_affects.how: A stay that pauses a contested personnel action can be extended while the board lacks enough members to act.
The Special Counsel can ask a remaining board member to extend a stay when the board has no quorum.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that take personnel actions
who_it_affects.how: Contested personnel actions may stay on hold for longer periods when the board cannot reach a quorum.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 27, 2017, and applies while the Merit Systems Protection Board lacks a quorum.
